Roy acts with little intelligence and self control throughout most of the movie. He's like a selfish, impetulant and irresponsible child that must be the first in line to get the latest Playstation in stores. He has an ‘Us and them’ mentality whereby if you weren't an actual UFO witness or some half-cracked alien conspiracy theorist he didn't care about what you said and law and order didn't exist. I think Roy is a big stain on a great movie. When you think about it, none of his actions benefited anyone. Jillian would've gotten back her son regardless if she went Devil's Tower or not and his discovery would amount to nothing because no one would believe him afterwards. He ruined his family all so he could see some cool alien stuff and weasel his way into the heart of a grieving single mom. His character is supposed to be redeemed by offering himself to the aliens. To me he is just this UFO geek that wanted to escape paying child support. Lacombe: Monsieur Neary. You can't go aboard zat space sheep. What about your madame and infants? Neary:……my work here is done.

What’s your relationship with alcohol? As a self-described connoisseur of fine liquor I have to honestly say that my relationship with alcohol has reached something of a close. In my mid to late 20s, when I started to drink habitually, one stiff drink used to give me a solid buzz/near drunkenness that lasted a couple hours. A 750ml bottle of rum, vodka, whisky or scotch with a chaser of choice could last me a month and change. However this frugality was because I had little alcohol tolerance and was prone to hangovers. Excessive drinking was not greatly desired unless I had friends over or something to celebrate. In my early to mid 30s, what I consider my peak age of drinking, two stiff drinks gave me a solid buzz and anything over that got me into the tipsy/drunken spectrum. This lasted about two hours at most and I had great tolerance. Hangovers ceased to exist for me, partially due to experience but mostly due to self discipline. However my urge to drink started growing and I started to feel come downs more strongly and frequently. Now I’m in my late 30s. It takes me three stiff drinks to get a solid buzz that lasts 30 minutes to an hour. After this my come down lasts practically the rest of the evening and lingers into the next day. The urges are so strong that sometimes the first place I'm drawn to in a grocery is the liquor section. A 750ml bottle wouldn't last me more than a week at the height of my urges. The funny thing about alcohol is that when I reach that peak whereby my buzz is at its strongest but I've not yet condescended into drunkenness, I feel as though I’ve manifested into my supreme self. It tricks me into thinking my mind operates deeper and much more efficiently under its influence. The day I found on my phone a ‘supreme self’ video recording I did of me slurring and rambling about deep, self discoveries through alcohol, it did me a favour and proved otherwise. I'm not a shitty person when I'm drunk. Nobody has a problem with me intoxicated. I've never become uncouth, aggressive or self destructive when I drink. I'm a shitty person during the come down. I become sullen, withdrawn and easily irritated. I lose sight of my goals and ambition and I tend to focus on all my disappointments in life which opens the floodgate to anxiety and depression. I've come to the stage where alcohol takes away a lot more than it gives. Yeah, the occasional beer or cocktail makes me feel relaxed, temporarily kicks out my fears and anxieties and can even give me a boost of confidence but now I’ve found myself at an odd stage in my life where my body is both desirous of alcohol and yet repelled by it. As such I've been weaning off of harder liquor and instead been having an occasional drink of my own homemade fruit wines when the urges come. My wines are admittedly less than stellar and with an alcohol percentage so low it makes Coors Light look like absinthe. However even though weaning from alcohol has stopped me from feeling like Alexander the Great for an hour or so, it sure beats feeling like Eeyore the Donkey for hours on end afterwards.

Do biracial people ever pick their white side and identify as white? Sigh The above photo shows five mixed raced men of varying ethnic makeup, myself included. What is the stupidest assumption you ever made? Several years ago I worked as a warehouse attendant for a major distribution company. It was my first job. Every year, usually in September, we had our annual stock-taking exercise. It was bittersweet because though it was hard work (especially for the males who did all the climbing and counting every single product in the warehouse whilst females wrote figures on the notepad) there would usually be a lot of the beautiful Head Office women present and we would be treated to lunch by the Director. We were all randomly assigned one partner. On our notice board they would put the name of our randomly allocated mystery partner. Of course many of the virile and single young men like myself hoped and prayed to be partnered with a stunning beauty from the Head Office. When the list was put up I saw that my partner was ‘Vanessa Milan.’ I jumped high into the air in excitement. VANESSA MILAN What a name! I envisioned a tanned beauty from a Mediterranean island, tall and shapely with arched eyebrows, a sensuous mouth and curly jet, black hair. In other words I imagined a Sophia Loren look-alike. I began bragging to my male friends that Vanessa Milan and I would probably be secretly in each others arms embracing behind a pallet of goods whilst they would be walking on eggshells with their nagging, old-maid partners. Every time I mentioned Vanessa Milan’s name I said it in a low whisper as though she were the Latin Goddess of Forbidden Love. ‘Vanessa Milan’ I drove my co-workers crazy uttering her exotic name every day. ‘Vanessa Milan’ I laughed at some of the names my friends were paired with: ‘Penny Thomas….Ha…..That sounds like a big, fat mama.’ ‘Giselle Aleong….she sounds like a bony psycho.’ And comments to that extent (I was 19 years old). One of my friends Rory advised me that I was a fool. That nothing could be more stupid than guessing what someone is like based on their name. I replied, ‘True, But a name like Vanessa Milan has to be an exotic beauty. Who ever heard a name like Vanessa Milan in this country?’ When the day came for the stock-take, all of us guys stood in the open area of the warehouse and observed a wide array of beauties from the Head Office. The Director gathered us all together for a prayer and then called out the names of the allocated partners for us to team up. Penny Thomas was a straight up knock-out. Giselle Aleong, with a body like that, could’ve graced the cover of Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Edition. I looked stunned as she walked by with my friend Rory (her assigned partner) who had warned me about my assumptions. He looked at me with a faint, mocking smile. When Vanessa Milan’s name was called, (the Director blasphemously screeched her name in her guttural voice) no one answered. All my friends stared at me as they were in great suspense to finally see this exotic mystery woman I boasted about all week. Suddenly, a dumpy, middle-aged lady with bad posture and Coke bottle specs that made her look like someone’s mom from the 60’s came hurriedly into the clearing. ‘I’m here. I’m here,’ she cried in a mournful voice. I was taken aback. Sophia Loren she wasn’t. She looked and acted more like Pat from the It’s Pat SNL sketch. Awkwardly I shook hands with her and stared at the ground. She began to relate a woeful tale of how she wasn’t feeling well that morning and was running late as she sped up the road driving but had forgotten to feed her dog so she had to drive back home and that was why she was late and on and on and on she went relating woeful, semi-depressing tales for me while we were doing our stock checks. ‘One hundred and seventy five cases of Diquez Baby Oil 125ml!’ I shouted down at her from a pallet of goods on the shelf above her, ‘Did you get that?’ ‘Oh sorry,’ she said, ‘I can’t hear you. I have bad hearing in my right ear. Ever since I was…..’ ‘ONE-SEVEN-FIVE CASES……DIQUEZ BABY OIL…….125ML, ‘ I shouted at the top of my lungs. This was the third time in thirty minutes this type of communication problem happened and I was getting frustrated. Part of it was my selfish and immature disappointment at her not being the beauty I imagined but alas she was so whiny and helpless. ‘I can’t hear you.’ she replied woefully, ‘I think we should go ask the Director if the Manager has any walky-talkies around.’ ‘WE DON’T HAVE ANY WALKY-TALKIES IN THE WAREHOUSE,’ I screamed at her but she already left to find the Director while I stood suspended 30 feet above the ground on a shelf waiting on her. In the end I had to count the stock and write in the figures myself as she followed me about apologizing at every turn. After the momentous day passed, for weeks my friends and co-workers would tease me. They would breathlessly whisper her name whenever I passed. ‘Vanessa Milan. Mi amore. Mi amore.’ Thus ended the saga of Vanessa Milan, My Latin Goddess of Forbidden Love.

What should I absolutely not do when visiting your country? TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO Avoid hiring 'local tour guides.’ Stick to official touring groups from your hotel or large hiking groups. You’ve come to Trinidad on a vacation but you don't want to be so 'touristy.’ You don't want to sign up for the generic cross country tour the hotel is offering. You don't want to be crammed in a bus with a bunch of khaki short wearing, middle aged couples who want to stop the bus every 10 minutes saying. 'Hey driver, look there's a natural spring there. I want to fill my water bottle.’ Or 'Ooh driver stop the bus. I want to get a picture of those local Trinidadian cows.’ And you definitely don't want to go on the same well beaten hiking track where ten buses like yours are parked so more tourists like yourself could commence on a 5 minute hike, past dozens of souvenir stalls, to see a dormant mud volcano which, if you're lucky, might belch out a nauseating scent of rotten eggs. It sounds awful but believe me the other option is far worse. You'd meet someone who'd tell you, 'I know a guy who does private tours. He'll take you to the real hidden sites that the tour groups don't go and he's very knowledgeable of history and professional. You don't have to stick with the dull tourist tours.’ You want to make the extra effort and discover the hidden Trinidad (or Tobago) and this guy sounds like the real deal. Here are the problems with that offer: Discovering a makeshift stone axe . My Scottish cousins realized this too late when they hired some guy who was a friend of a friend of friend who did private tours. He was taking them to Turure Water Steps which was indeed a beautiful place with four amazing waterfalls, each bigger than the last. When I heard he was charging $1000 TT (roughly 150 US) to take them there I protested and told them that they were being ripped off. Anyone could take them there for free. They argued that he was a professional and had deep knowledge of the history of places. I went along with them for the trip. Some hours later, returning home, they agreed that they were ripped off. In summary the lesson learned here is that there are several people like that so-called tour guide who wants to rip off hapless tourists. Either you stick with your hotel tour or if you want to go off the beaten track, join a professional hiking/tour group or go with a large group of friendly, trustworthy locals. Doing otherwise could have you ripped off or even worse. Edit 31.08.21 Had no idea this little tidbit of info would've garnered so many upvotes. Thank you all for the support. When did you think, "this can only be a fake"? While employed as a pizza delivery rider, after the lifting of the COVID lock-down, our company decided to pull a fast one. A memo from the head office was circulated among all restaurant staff at all branches. It basically said that the company was so concerned about our welfare in these trying times that they were willing to keep a percentage of our weekly salary for us as a form of savings. The memo also mentioned that if we agreed to this ‘Pizza Savings’ (my term, not theirs) that we will be getting 0% interest. My delivery co-worker and I had a field day with that memo. We read it several times in disbelief and laughed. The owners could not be serious. It was obvious they wanted to get a loan/invest in something. It was as if they told themselves instead of taking a 16% interest loan from the bank why not simply take it from their uneducated restaurant workers, all they needed was our signatures. I went around some of the co-workers joking about it. Most of us laughed it off but two of them couldn’t understand what was so funny. ‘But we’re getting 0% interest!’ an older woman working the grill said. She seemed to have the idea that this was a good thing. Apparently she had had so many loans in the past that to her the word interest = bad. I explained to her it was a savings and not a loan. That with savings you want the highest interest you could get and the exact opposite when it comes to a loan. ‘But isn’t it good to have a savings?’ one of the teenaged girls working the pizza table said. I explained to her it is a good thing but it makes no sense to save your money with someone giving you 0%. I tried explaining how banks work, about buying shares etc and getting the best rates for your money. Both women looked at me in silence. In the end they both decided to ‘try it out.’ I didn't know what shocked me more. The fact that the restaurant attempted that stunt or the fact that it actually worked on two employees. Edit: Are you ready to invest in your Pizza Savings Fund? 0% interest guaranteed and you can be assured your money is so safe with us that no one can touch it, not even you. What was the most disgusting thing you have seen at an auto mechanic shop? This may be cheating a bit but it actually occurred at an auto-electrician's garage. The guys who ran this garage were really nice. And I'm not just saying that as a form of courtesy. They were eerily pleasant to the point that I wondered if they were on some sort of drug or followers of some type of underground Eastern philiosphy/religion. They would never get impatient or irritated with you. There was a calming resonance in their voice that made you feel everything was going to be OK and they would listen to you with the utmost sympathy and understanding. Sometimes I would find myself wanting to visit them even though I had no electrical issues with my vehicle, just to bask in their warmth and friendliness. They were experts at their job too. As one would expect they were quite popular in the area. You would line up for hours to get a spot inside but it was worth it. Absolutely no one who was familiar with them would haggle, speak condescendingly towards or show any form of bad face towards them. That would be like sacrilege. However one guy had to be the one to disrupt the positive energy coming from our beloved hippie electrical-garage commune. In Trinidad we have this phenomenon called ‘wetman.’ A wetman is usually a vain but ignorant young man who thrives on attention. His life revolves around impressing easy women with a show of careless spending, flashy clothes and the official wetman badge of honour, his Nissan Tiida vehicle. For some inexplicable reason this vehicle is coveted by wetmen throughout the country, most likely due to the fact that it is one of the cheapest (foreign used) sedans available. Wetmen are also known to be notoriously cheap, uncouth and many of them live such a flagrantly hedonistic lifestyle, they are forced to secretly live in their Nissan Tiidas. In other words, a wetman is a scoundrel. One faithful day, a wetman joined the queue that we would form by parking outside the garage on a little road alongside the garage. In typical wetman fashion he had his gangsta music blasting at full volume the entire time he was parked. One of the apprentices would habitually pass to check on each person lined up outside to ask what was their problem. Doing this, they would find out who had simple problems that could be fixed at an instant, so he/she could be dealt with immediately and speeden the process. The apprentice went to the wetman who was blasting his music. The wetman only slightly lowered the volume to communicate with the apprentice. The apprentice had to tell the wetman to lower the music some more so he could hear him, which irritated the wetman. ‘My car giving trouble,’ Wetman said, ‘Everytime I switch off I have to ask someone for a jump start to start it back.’ The apprentice pulled out his multimeter and said, ‘Switch off the vehicle and lift the bonnet.’ The wetman scowled and in a venemous tone replied, ‘Brother. Like you not listening to what I saying? Switch off? You expect me to push this car all the way inside your garage?’ I was behind the wetman in the queue I was aghast at how stupid he was. Didn't he realize he was speaking to an actual electrician? Didn't he realize that the apprentice would find a way to get it started again? Wisely, the apprentice decided it was not worth it explaining all that to him and told him to wait until he gets a space inside the garage and the boss would personally deal with his vehicle. Wetman then resumed blasting his music much to the displeasure of myself and the apprentice who was now trying to ask me as to what was the issue I had. The apprentice had to go back over to the wetman and tell him again to lower the volume. ‘What da f**k boy,’ the wetman cried, ‘You all taking so damn long here and I can't listen to my tunes.’ He kept threatening to leave and I was hoping for him to make good on his threat but to my disappointment he remained. A half hour later we are both inside the garage. Realizing that the wetman was trouble, the apprentice wisely went to fetch the boss to deal with him. The boss arrived and Wetman stood outside his vehicle with arms folded. The engine was still running but the bonnet was lifted. Wetman squinted at the engine as though looking for some creature hiding somewhere that was causing his electrical problem. The boss approached and asked him what was the matter. Wetman scowled and replied, ‘I done tell yuh secretary what is the problem. Like you all dumb inside here?’ At that moment everyone's head turned towards Wetman's direction. Someone had blasphemed our precious garage! Everyone waited to see how the boss would handle it. No one ever witnessed any of the electricians lose their cool, especially the boss who was the kindest and most calm of them all. ‘Yes,’ the boss replied without any change of tone ‘Mike told me that you're getting ignition problems. I was just hoping to get some more information so I could know the best way to approach the problem.’ ‘The car not starting,’ Wetman uttered irritatedly, ‘What else you need to know? You is the electrician, not me. A whole hour I waiting outside, I going to lose out on a job I was getting.’ He then did what we Trinis call ‘steups’ which is the noise poorly raised people make to show disgust by sucking spit through your teeth. ‘Switch off the ignition let me run the tester through.’ Again Wetman's face scowled and he got defensive, ‘Brother,’ he growled, ‘I not switching off my engine. Last man I went by make me switch off the engine. He couldn’t fix my problem and I had to push my car out the road and ask someone for a jumpstart. That is failure. You have to fix my problem with the engine running!’ The boss stared at the apprentice and then glanced at the Wetman, who was clearly of a legendary level of stupidity as he stood there defiant and folding his arms. How is the boss going to deal with this one? Everyone was probably thinking the latter question. ‘I understand,’ said the boss calmly, ‘However if we operate on your vehicle while it's running we could destroy your circuits. The danger…’ The boss then paused for second and said, ‘Next Monday is the best day for you to come. We're getting a device that can work on vehicles while the engine is running without damaging anything. It's being shipped from China so give me a call Sunday evening to confirm when you're coming.’ Like magic, the little white lie worked and wetman accepted and left in a hurry to see about his hired job. Everyone breathed a sigh of relief when the ignoramus left. The next time I came, I enquired about the I individual and they happily informed me that someone must've solved Wetman's problem because he never did call or show up again. Or maybe he was offered a starring role in the movie below.

What is the scariest moment you have had in your own home? This is a roughly 6 feet deep hole that I had dug in my front yard some years ago. It is dug to insert an electrical power pole and concrete and stones are poured to keep it in place. Doesn't it seem like a fun idea to play Rambo and jump in such a hole, cover it with dead leaves and braches and jump out to scare anyone who visits you? That's just the movies and no I did not do anything so silly. But in reality, you could possibly die by jumping into a narrow 6 feet deep hole. I say this because it almost happened to me: Here in the Tropics we have the dry season and the rainy season. I don't think I need to explain the difference. However in the rainy season we tend to get what is called the Hurricane season which is a period that characterizes long and heavy rain, thunderstorms and the occasional flash flood. My area is prone to flooding. This a view of my front yard and the road during an average Hurricane Season flood. (The pole at the center-right is where the hole was located.) My hole was dug during the dry season. However the not-too-wholesome electrician I hired who was to put in the pole delayed the job for months upon months until hurricane season reached. One day, I heard a faint squeaking noise coming from the hole. I looked in to see a cute little mouse fighting to survive in the 8 inches of water that remained in the hole due to rain. I couldn't help but feel sorry for the little bugger so I grabbed a piece of wood and stretched it towards it, thinking the mouse would gladly hop onto the wood and allow me to save him. It turns out the mouse would rather take its chances drowning. I had half the mind to leave the stupid creature to drown but my heart got the better of me and I decided to jump in and fetch the mouse by hand. I got in, carefully avoiding stepping on the creature. It was quite muddy at the base and hard to move because it was mostly clay. I picked up the little mouse and carefully extended my hand out of the hole and dropped him lightly on the surface where I would assume he scuttled off in great appreciation of me. I then tried hoisting myself out. However the entire area was slippery due to last night's showers. I couldn't get a good grip on anything due to the slipperiness, the lack of room to maneuver and because my feet kept getting stuck deep in the mud where I stood. I tried for several times but to no avail. I had no idea that this little hole would be such a challenge. Mind you I'm only 5’ 10 and don't have the wingspan of Michael Phelps. Regardless if I did, everywhere I gripped my hand slid on the clay mud. After several attempts my energy was depleted. Suddenly thunder boomed and a heavy rain started. My heart began to pulse. I realized that I could quite possibly drown here; if not from the rain filling this hole up then the possible flood afterwards. I yelled for help a few times but to no luck, the sound of heavy rain was competing with my yells. The only chance of anyone hearing me was if someone happened to be walking the road nearby. What are the chances of someone casually walking the road during a thunderstorm? I had to get out of this simple hole or drown like my mouse friend almost did. What a dumb way to die I might add. The water level in the hole was beginning to rise towards my knees. In a frenzied fit of desperation I found some reserve of energy and my brain started to click. I undid my mud soaked shoes which was causing additional heaviness, threw them out and like a cat on steroids I simply grabbed and flailed at the four walls with my hands, feet and back until I somehow managed to get a grip and lift myself out. Some fingers and parts of my back were bleeding from contact with sharp stones. I looked as though I just survived D-Day Normandy when all I did was come out of a small, muddy hole; an idiot who almost died saving a mouse. So take it from me if you want to live a long fulfilling life. Don't jump into muddy 6 feet deep holes, especially during Hurricane season. Edit: Wow I'm actually getting upvotes for this. You all care about my life. That's sweet. Here is another mouse (or could very well be the same one) I befriended during a flood a few weeks later. Edit 2: Many commenters are suggesting that I should've simply allowed the water in the hole to rise and simply float/paddle my way to the surface. Please. By all means, if this bizarre situation ever happens to you do not wait for that possibility. This wasn't a tiled pool but a muddy hole more narrow than a coffin. You can drown trying to free your feet from the thick, viscous clay mud that envelops your feet and the fact that your arms and legs have limited motion. Scream for help as best as you can and if that fails get your arse out of that hole by whatever means but do not wait for the water to rise on you. You might as well be buried there the following day.

What is the best album with the worst album cover? There are so many great albums out there with terrible album covers that I can’t commit to just listing one. Sorry. If you want to seem like an intellectual hipster who is aware of global issues, look no further than Manic Street Preachers - Everything Must Go. A stunning album that perfect encapsulates that mid-late 90’s arena rock vibe. The album is epic in its scope and profound in its heavy subject matter: loneliness, international crises, suicide, class struggle etc. It was such an underwhelming experience to see the cover as nothing more than three passport photos pasted on a design that looked like a Microsoft Paint project. MGMT - Congratulations (2010) What a great album. MGMT’s music takes you back to the heights of psychedelic pop and prog-rock of the late 60s and 70s. Siberian Breaks is a 12 minute modern day masterpiece. This is one of the generic and unpleasant album covers I’ve ever come across in recent history. The band members are weird and their music videos are beyond bizarre but this artwork looks like some cut and paste crap done by a stoner wannabe with no talent. What is it about the late 80s and early 90s that excessively loud and garish was the aesthetic for everything. Of these three funk metal bands I’d go with Faith No More - The Real Thing by a long shot. But what is that on the album cover? A fire-breathing clam? An oil baron’s mind after taking LSD? God alone knows. Jeff Buckley - Grace If there’s one thing that prevents me from buying/listening to an album, it’s when the album shows the artist’s pretty face trying to look all deep. I would’ve passed this album straight in a record store and assume it’s another one of Josh Groban’s senior-citizen friendly collection of soul covers. I would’ve never guessed the album to be the greatest debut album in the history of rock music. But what’s wrong with this album cover? Black Sabbath’s debut actually has a really good album cover, if not one of the greatest. I put it there to compare with Black Sabbath’s second album’s cover. Both albums were made in 1970. However Paranoid was recorded four months after Black Sabbath to capitalize on the growing popularity. The cover speaks for itself in all honesty. AND THE AWARD FOR THE GREATEST BAND WITH THE WORST ALBUM COVERS GOES TO . . . . . It’s a tie between Pantera and The Grateful Dead Garish, corny, ugly, sleazy are just a few of the adjectives I can think of whenever I see an album from either critically acclaimed bands. Pantera’s covers opt to be as stupidly macho as possible (on a budget) whilst Grateful Dead seem to look for the cheesiest of cheese. But never judge a book (or album) by it’s cover. All the above albums are worth a listen.

What is the shortest amount of time that you spent at a job? How old were you? Why did you quit? 8 hours. I worked for one of the most prestigious cinema multiplexes in Trinidad and Tobago. I had quit my job at the warehouse in an attempt to enter the world of selling life insurance. That didn't work out and pretty soon I desperately needed a job as I was flat broke. I applied to work as a cashier in the multiplex cinema. I always loved their aesthetics and felt as though they really cared about what they did and the people they hired. That couldn't be further from the truth. I was young, a few months shy of 23, but still most of my coworkers were several years younger than me, typically the teenager fresh out of high school looking for their first job. Practically all my co-workers were males and our supervisor was an attractive girl in her mid 20s who had a talent for making us guys feel as though we were scoring points with her and that it was only a matter of time before she would agree to a date. In retrospect I believe this was a tactic she used to keep us from leaving prematurely. With me she directly assisted in dressing me in my uniform and when my trousers was missing a zip, she made flirtatious comments while helping me apply double sided tape on my crotch. I sincerely thought we were going to hit it off until I saw that she responded positively to all the other guys flirtations. This one stocky guy, not very bright, made subtle threats to me that I stay away from her; that he had it in the bag and I'd best go and mind my own business. I was put to train under this kid who couldn't be older than 17. He was openly gay and had an aptitude for being quite helpful. He explained to me that in the cash booth there were no stools for us to sit on. We had to stand the entire 6 — 10 hrs because the company believed that sitting causes idleness which in turn causes mistakes to be made. I told him that that was a shitty arrangement for us cashiers. He agreed but explained to me that he was here just for the summer so it didn't bother him. To this day I've never seen a more effective cashier than that 17 year old boy I met briefly at MovieTowne. He treated the cash he recieved lovingly and would go as far as putting the dirty bills at the back of the pile so that his drawer would look full of crisp new bills. I don't know if that gave him some sense of satisfaction in life but it was quite interesting to watch him. Pretty soon I realized that the cinema was flooded with managers. They seemed to come out of the woodwork. Every shift had a different manager who periodically came and collected the cash whenever it reached a certain amount. While doing this they kept making these ambiguous statements that basically said, 'If even a dime is short we're gonna have your ass for breakfast.’ When it was lunch break I headed over to the concessions booth and to the ushers to make friends. A manager leaped out of nowhere in front of me and told me that I'm not allowed to mingle with other departments. I managed to evade him and strike a conversation with a young female usher. I asked what was the problem with this place and she explained that she felt sorry for cashiers. Managers didn't trust them and always felt as though the new cashiers were trying to find ways to rob the cinema. They basically wanted cashiers isolated from everyone to prevent any kind of 'cahoots’ situation. I was given 15 minutes for my lunch break and within 10 minutes this burly, bald guy was on the hunt for me to be getting back to my post. He was the head honcho manager of that branch of the cinema. Something about him irked me greatly and I could see he had similar sentiments every time our eyes met. That evening was very busy. Terminator: Salvation had had its premier and long lines of patrons came to see it. The cinema had a long list of random discounts and promotions; senior citizens discount, student discounts, free birthday specials, discounts for members of the defense force, discounts for friends of animal shelters, radio promotion discounts etc etc. Even though it was my first day I was expected to learn how to cash all these discounts properly. At the end of my shift, Mr. Baldy came with a smug look on his face explaining to me that I didn't collect two coupons for senior citizens and as such my cash register was short by $80. He explained that this would be deducted from my salary which meant that I worked for $50 that day ($25 of which was spent on getting taxis to and from there and the remainder was spent on lunch). In other words I stood all day on my feet cashing so I could buy myself some lunch. Mr. Baldy then has the audacity to tell me that I'll be working a double tomorrow of which he asserts that it would be good for me to recuperate the money I lost today. I went home a heavy heart. I only spent 8 hrs at the job but already I despised it. However, good fortune was directed my way. My mother gave me a letter that explained that I had an interview for a much more comfortable job with a better salary. I had the choice of going back to Baldy and Madame Psudo-Flirty or going for the job interview. You could guess which option I chose. Edit: This is one of three working-in-a-cinema related stories I have thus far. The other two are much more funny and inspirational and can be read here and here

Do you feel uncomfortable at work around certain co-workers? If so, why? There’s a running joke on online chat-rooms and forums about people who look like created players. If you are/were an avid gamer you would get the joke instantly. If you aren’t then a created player is when gamers have the option of creating their own customized player i.e. choosing their skin colour, height, hairstyle, weight, clothes etc. Many gamers attempt to make the most random or disturbing looking player possible just for kicks e.g huge head, clown hair, wide apart eyes, inhuman skin tone etc. In the real world, it’s hardly likely you would come across anyone looking like these guys anytime soon but on the rare occasion that you do, you tell yourself, ‘Hey! That guy looks like a created player!’ Frivolity out of the way, there’s a man in my workplace who is like a created player. He’s not eerie looking but he is eerie in that no one can could put a finger on his personality without using the word ‘random.’ One day he would swagger to work looking as though he stepped off the set of a poor man’s Western movie, complete with snakeskin cowboy boots, cowboy hat, shirt opened up at the chest and RayBan shades (we work in a school by the way). Another day he would come dressed overly modest as though he spent the summer with monks in Tibet with a head shaved bald, large flowing shirt and giving an aura of calm resolve. Then another day would be a day of espionage as he would be dressed incognito and would spend the day peeping from behind a newspaper at God knows what. If you try to talk to him, you leave with a feeling of discomforting bewilderment. You would ask him a basic, ‘How did you spend your weekend?’ and he would start talking about why every teenager nearing adulthood should practice Feng Shui. Or He would come to you with an angry rant about why he will not teach any unvaccinated students while he himself isn’t vaccinated and hardly wears his masks. Or He would speak ill of teachers who come late to school while he himself has an abysmal regularity and punctuality rate. Everything about him is just random and contradictory. No one knows what he’s up to where he came from and where he’s going. But for me, though it’s uncomfortable to communicate with him, it’s fun to see the ultimate, living breathing created player.

What screams "I'm low class"? A girl, no older than 20 comes into Papa John's a busy Friday evening. I'm helping out at the cash register. It's near the end of the month (pay day for most people) and this is when we get our bulk of orders. The phone is ringing off the hook. I'm really just a delivery guy but the store is short staffed so I help cash. The girl, her cellphone tucked at her groin area in her trousers comes up to me at the register. Totally ignoring the fact that I'm taking an order on the phone she proceeds to talk about what she wants. I paused from the phone call to tell her, ‘One minute please miss I'm on the phone with a customer.’ I look as her eyebrows slant further downwards in anger and she puts her arms on her hips, staring at me in a show of impatience. When I finished with the call I apologized and asked what would she like. ‘Gimme one of the chicken pizzas.’ The phone started ringing again. I sighed inwardly. All the time she spent staring at me in anger she didn't even make up her mind as to what she wanted. ‘Which one of the chicken pizzas?’ I don't know if by asking a simple question like that she found some measure of offense but she replied in a belligerent tone, ‘How am I supposed to know what chicken pizzas you have?’ The phone continued ringing. I sighed again. I pointed to the display above her head and told her I have to take the call, choose a pizza by the time. Instead she frowns at me while I take another phone order, she refusing to look at the menu board herself. When I was done she glared at me and said, ‘Chicken and pine….the largest size you have.’ ‘That would be an extra large’ I said. ‘I know!’ she spat. She then proceeds to take out of her purse a brown envelope which contained the salary she just received from whatever job she worked. She proudly counts her 100s in front of me and gave me $200 without waiting for me to tell her the price of her order. I gave her her change and receipt and told her the waiting time (15–20 mins). She proceeded to stare at me whilst I take other orders, helped cut pizzas from off the oven and organized my deliveries at the same time. With her seeing me doing all these things at once I thought she would have generated some sympathy for me seeing that I wasn't really the cashier but just a delivery guy helping out the situation. While heading towards the exit with my deliveries I passed near her and she beckons me. I thought it was to apologize for her attitude. Instead she tells me something that makes my blood boil instantly. ‘Ummm. How much longer for my order?’ She just placed her order 5 minutes ago! I gritted me teeth and replied, ‘It’s not in the oven yet. 10 to 15 minutes.’ She rolled her eyes and looked away. I then realize what her game was. She didn't really care about the pizza. Her fetish was to feel some sort of superiority over someone else and the only place she could achieve that was in a fast food restaurant. We get customers like that regularly, especially around month's end (pay day). They get some kind of sick thrill out of pissing people off and flaunting what (little) money they have. So to answer the question above, nothing screams 'I’m low class’ more than people who buy fast food for the sake of showing off/putting on airs.

Would Hollywood actor Brad Pitt have made it in old or classic Hollywood back in the day? Very interesting question. For the sake of simplification let's just assume that by Classic Hollywood you mean the Hays Code era of Hollywood whereas sex, nudity, graphic violence, rape etc could not be demonstrated in Hollywood films. (1934 — 1968) 1930s — 1940s Hollywood Hollywood in the aftermath of the Great Depression and the outbreak of the Second World War. This is the age of the Go-Getter and although silent movies are now obsolete, it's exaggerative stage acting style is still rampant. Audiences of this era are favorable towards a certain type of male screen presence. Popular actors of the era are mostly an embodiment of what were considered desirable, manly traits. This is the era of Clark Gable, Cary Grant, Gary Cooper, James Stewart, Errol Flynn, John Wayne and Henry Fonda. The archetypal male film star was usually tall (over 6 feet), athletic, handsome, possessing a rich and resonant voice and possessing a certain self assured alpha male quality. The kind of man who would've made a great career as a top salesman or workforce motivator. The nation was wounded after two World Wars and these idealistic tropes were coveted by men and women alike. It was an age that was obsessively preoccupied with courage, persistence and survival. It was the era of sucking in your emotions and holding your chin high. Unless in possession of exemplary acting skills or song and dance expertise, actors who lacked several of these traits were relegated to minor supporting roles, comic relief roles, extras, stunt work or failed to make it in the film industry at all. Despite being ruggedly handsome, Brad Pitt would've had a hard time getting work in Hollywood during this era. He did not fit the height requirement, his voice would not be considered rich and animated and his brooding, sombre presence would've been a turn off for a national audience hungry for the next cocky, high shouldered, go-getting macho man. 1950s Hollywood The ideal aforementioned leading man is still prevalent with Charlton Heston, Gregory Peck, Burt Lancaster, and Rock Hudson maintaining the status quo. However standards are less rigid as actors like William Holden, Frank Sinatra, Kirk Douglas, Yul Brynner and Tony Curtis, who have the macho appeal but lack the height, are some of the top stars. A growing interest in brooding more sensitive type 'method' acting is gaining ground with the likes of James Dean, Marlon Brando and Paul Newman. Brad Pitt would've been better able to find work in such type roles but the competition would be fierce and only those with extensive stage experience and schooled in New York at the Actor's Studio would get top priority over some quiet, good looking guy from Missouri. 1960s Hollywood The growing counterculture revolution is finally making an impact on Hollywood. While the war scarred older generation is fading to make way for the Baby Boomers, the conservative values and ideal macho leading man is no longer as appealing for those hungry for emotional catharsis. The audience is yearning for a leading man who they could relate to, who shares their flaws and can demonstrate vulnerability. Even the more macho type actors are expected to demonstate weakness and more sensitivity. These would include Clint Eastwood, Sean Connery, Charles Bronson, Steve McQueen, Robert Redford, George Kennedy and Rod Steiger. Slurred speaking (Marlon Brando), meek voiced (Eastwood) overweight (Steiger) and short stature (Bronson) are traits no longer shunned by Hollywood elite. Brad Pitt would've found the greatest chance of obtaining prominent roles during this era. Who knows he might've even replaced Robert Redford in Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid.

What is an unpopular opinion you hold? Self-Help Books Can Actually Ruin Your Life Especially if you come from a developing country. Have you ever sat and pondered as to the staggering amount of self-help authors there are out there? It seems every week someone is recommending to you some brand new, groundbreaking, best selling title that eschews a whole new perspective on how to view the world and live your life. The problem with 99% of the authors: Are they really living their dreams? Or are they making a living selling dreams? Moulding a life of success, solely based on easily digestible tips, hints and formulae is like solving advanced level algebra, whilst riding a roller coaster, using only your knowledge of multiplication tables. The knowledge can help….you probably might get the most simple problems correct……but it would be ridiculous to think that you would be able to solve all your problems in that manner, under those unique circumstances. These are people living in dire poverty in India. What can I do to help them out of this financial rut?….. I know! Think and Grow Rich by Napoleon Hill A lonely, mentally unhinged taxi driver… That's easy. The Road Less Travelled and How to Win Friends and Influence People. A wealthy but socially and emotionally void and suicidal philanthropist. Hmm. That's a tough one….The Alchemist by Paolo Coelho and you can throw in The Prophet by Gibran as well. Nothing cures rich-man depression more than obscure but romanticised Eastern parables and fables. Ok, so it's foolish to try and live according to a self help book, but how can I ruin my life simply by seeking advice? In every job that I've worked, every year there's always that one newly employed guy who is all jacked up from reading a lifetime's supply of self help books. He is always brimming with confidence and eager to pin his obstacles against the ropes and send failure scattering with his 2000 watt grin. He hates to hear no and scorns to see people second guessing themselves. He wants to take on all life's challenges and has a Napoleon Hill or Robert Kiyosaki quote ready for every situation. Then something inexplicable happens. Something gradually builds up, registers in his subconscious and overflows upon his ego. It usually takes the form of this mental conversation. 'Wait a minute. I've done everything the book advised me to. I've followed the instructions to the hilt…….yet I'm not seeing the results.’ He hasn't been promoted by his supervisor, rather his supervisor has been taking credit for his own efforts and is getting the promotion instead. Despite constantly showing support and empathy, his wife is even more nagging and helpless than when he first met her. His dedication to go above and beyond with the customer now has him doing the workload of all the lazy and incompetent coworkers around him, who still draw the same salary. He gets the lion's share of verbal abuse from disgruntled customers who rather voice their issues with him rather than the incompetent coworkers. His small business as a landscaper is suffering because his fair price is being exploited whilst mediocre landscapers are charging abominably overpriced rates and are getting more work than him. What the hell is happening here? He followed some great and timeless advice. He just forget to put in one small factor in his equation. His personal environment. His ever changing, ever complex, personal environment. The variable that if included onto his scientific calculator would produce the answer E or 'Error.’ In developing countries likes Trinidad, using US or English or German translated or Dutch translated or any developed country self help books can cause ruin your life because the environment is so different. In developing countries: These are all factors that contradict with what he read in his books and come only through experience. Had he been all the wiser he would've known that not every bit of advice in his self help books could be applied to his unique situation and environment. To make matters worse nowadays, everybody is a self help author and rather than have synchronized, compatible, time tested advice, we have polarising, wishy-washy, one-size-fits-all concoctions and psudo-psychological, parabolic gibberish. Basically, self help authors write anecdotes that's easy to understand, easy to apply and appealing to the majority. Below is a list of a few popular modern self help authors and their most famous philosophy: Robert Kiyosaki: If you have to lose, lose spectacularly. Malcolm Gladwell: You have within you an instinct to know when something 'feels’ like a rip-off. Jay Shetty: Think like a monk. Deepak Chopak: Thinking is like brain chemistry. Steve Harvey: Act like a lady, think like a man Paolo Coelho: The universe…

What show / movie had no right to be as good as it was? Back in 1999 my brother and I was spending some summer vacation time at our cousin's place in Tobago. It wasn't the greatest of vacations because our cousin and her boyfriend were having these vicious fights over money (they weren't in the best place financially and had four daughters below the age of 5). We decided to spend a Saturday afternoon going to the cinema. We didn't care what was on, we just wanted to get away from the endless arguments amidst the chaos of screaming toddlers and mounds of filthy diapers. This was the double feature of the weekend: As a pair of hormone raging, ignorant and slightly sexist teenage boys, you could guess which movie appealed to us more. We were grateful that the 007 movie was showing first so we wouldn't have to stick around to watch Double Jeopardy or as my brother called it The Fugitive….but with a Woman. When The World Was Not Enough ended with its typical 007 sexual innuendo type final scene my brother and I looked at each other and nodded. It was ok. There was a lot of explosions, chase scenes, Denise Richards’ bouncing breasts and shorty shorts but we both knew we were unimpressed. However, in our typical peer influenced macho-vision we pretended that the movie was the real deal. We had the choice of watching Ashley Judd outrun a police car or go home and face adults yelling while half naked toddlers pee themselves in fright. We decided to watch the movie. What a great decisions that was. Double Jeopardy was like a roller coaster ride that got better by the minute. It was far better than The World is Not Enough. It was even better than The Fugitive. When she got her poetic justice in the end my brother and I jumped from our seats and wanted to hug each other in tears. We could give a fart about our macho ideals, Ashley Judd was our sister and she finally been done right. It was that good of a movie! We left the cinema thoroughly satisfied and entertained in so much that the choas that awaited us home didn't seem to matter anymore. I recently rewatched it with the idea that maybe it wasn't that great and maybe because we were dumb teenagers it had made an impression. I was blown away even moreso a thirty something year old dad than as a thirteen year old boy. The movie abandons every cliche there is about on-the-run and fugitive type action thrillers. The lead role is no superhero, there is no stupid forced comic relief character making racist jokes, there is no romantic subplot. Straight up escape and revenge served on a hot plate with Tommy Lee Jones in his best performance ever imho. I sincerely recommend it.

Was Shelley Duvall considered attractive? When I was a boy growing up, this character was the epitome of ‘attractive’ among boys my age: This was the exact opposite: Now that I'm a full grown adult I find it odd that my attraction has reversed. Nowadays I would consider prime Shelley Duvall far more attractive than prime Pamela Anderson. I'm not saying this as a form of virtue signalling due to her sad passing. I've observed photos from her in the past and discovered that she possessed a very unique beauty. This beauty was exploited quite often in her roles and modeling in the 1970s. Sadly she was only given frumpy housewife and plain Jane supporting roles into the 80s and 90s and all but disappeared at the turn of the millenium, only resurfacing for that infamous Dr. Phil interview in 2016. Despite being tall and thin, with big ears and eyes and crooked teeth Shelley Duvall’s looks were all natural. This might be my personal opinion but she seemed to possess a certain humility about her; the kind of person who wouldn't put on airs about herself and be friendly to almost anyone. Pamela Anderson’s beauty involved a lot of plastic surgery, hair dye and excessive makeup. To each his own but in a hypothetical party full of people I'd make a bee line to be the first to offer a drink to Shelley Duvall. Then we'd talk, sit and laugh at all the hopelessly shallow guys flocking around Pamela Anderson at the other end of the room. RIP

What is that one picture that describes the lowest point in your life? Sometime in April 2015 I used to be one of those who believed that depression was a hackneyed excuse, lazy people used as a defence mechanism. I believed that any mental struggle could be conquered on a mind-over-matter basis. My extended family was prone to bouts of depression and bipolar disorder and I would always roll my eyes when I heard them speak of their troubles and how it has affected their lives. At age 28 my girlfriend became pregnant. It was not planned. Prior to this announcement we were sharing a modest apartment and no matter how much I tightened my belt I couldn't overcome experiencing great financial difficulties. Besides my day job I also got an income doing transport and lawn maintenance. Soon my vehicle started giving me no end of troubles and I could no longer spend money fixing it so I left it to rot. My credit card was maxed out and I was owing money to some of my friends. After paying rent I could barely afford groceries. My financial woes caused me to lose contact with my friends so when she and I argued (which was every week) and she stormed out, I was left destitute and lonely in a shabby apartment complex, no one and nowhere to turn. During one of these episodes, like an awful aftertaste, a notion came into my mind. You've made a big mistake. You're going to f**k this child's life up . I tried to laugh away the notion but it buzzed around my mind like some sort of devilish fairy. You’re just another deadbeat father who can't get it right. I started pacing around trying to get this notion out of my mind. My heart raced and my nerves were on edge. My head felt light and heavy at the same time. You've made such a big mistake. What the hell were you thinking? I took deep breaths and attempted to think positive thoughts. Then as though a floodgate was released, it came: panic attacks. I felt these strange sensations in my skin, these popping, spasmic sensations similar to the plastic bubbles that wrap your delivery that you pop unconsciously with your fingers. It was completely overwhelming. I sat down to try and breathe it away, mind-over-matter as I used to preach but it simply gave way to what I can only describe as the feeling of a heavy, stifling bog taking residence in my brain. It was depression. My back hunched over as my mind felt clogged and lifeless. I couldn't stop thinking of my problems and asking myself interrogative questions. I sat down in defeat, fearful for anyone to see me like this, fearful for the phone to ring. The worst thing about depression is that it tricks you into believing that your life was always a series of tragedy and sorrow, that this is how things are and has always been. It was as though my positive emotions and memories were locked away in a cellar, unrecognizable in an iron mask. I felt like a burden and a drain on other people's happiness. When I saw other people happy and proactive it only reminded me of how unhappy and useless I was. These sensations would usually happen during sunsets for some strange reason. My appetite was all but gone so was my passions and interests. At its peak I became emaciated, 30–40 pounds lighter than my usual self. This feeling came on a daily basis, first with a dose of panic attacks then sinking into that low, rotting, depressed feeling where my face literally looked like Eeyore from Winnie the Pooh. I would record my suicidal feelings on a rating from 1 to 10 and on many days I would record myself as high as 9. After my daughter was born I was terrified of getting the male version of post partum depression. Thankfully, I was lucky, the depression wasn't chronic and it waned to a point where only once a week I got those horrid familiar feelings but of a lesser intensity. After a year I was healthy enough to take up a second job, clear my debts and provide for my daughter whilst my mental demons were held at bay. Today, I am in a much better place mentally and financially. Not going to brag but I think I've accomplished a bit since depression first reared its ugly head seven years ago. However, it's comes back every now and again. Like a unwanted vagabond it shows up at my doorstep, bedraggled and defeated, but not yet dead and it stops me in my tracks to give me a taste of those familiar feelings of the past, (usually during sunsets). Depression is no joke. If you know someone who demonstrates any symptoms/behaviours such as I had/did, try your best to assist that person, without overwhelming them with pity and making a huge fuss. Be patient with such a person without coming across as though they are helpless. Just play it cool. Edit 21.01.22. Depression and other mental illnesses play a great role in relationships and with families. It is very difficult to be in a relationship with a spouse who suffers from mental illness. It can cause severe problems for future generations. Click here to read how it.

What was your first clue you were no longer as young as you thought you were? While working in a school library I was at the computers assisting some students in finishing their assignments to submit to their teachers. Most students would email their assignments to their teacher, others (who didn't have/couldn't remember their email address) would save it on a USB flash drive . This one student who had neither an email address or a flash drive raised his hand for assistance and told me of his situation. I went into our storage cupboard and brought out an old rewritable CD-RW; the kind I used back in school to copy (‘burn’ as we used to call it) data onto. I gave him the shiny disc and walked off assuming that he knew what to do with it. ‘Sir!’ I heard his voice call after me. ‘Yeah?’ ‘What am I supposed to do with this?’ ‘Burn it,’ I said and looked at him stoically. His friends started laughing believing that I was teasing. ‘Sir stop joking. I need to save my work.’ ‘Burn the work onto the CD’ I said and he started to look at me irritated. ‘Sir help him out. Stop joking’ one of the friends said. It then dawned on me that they had no idea what ‘burning a CD’ was. This was before their time. I proceeded to demonstrate to them how to copy data onto a CD-RW, feeling like a crusty old man giving them a tour on a private railroad. The sad thing was they were all 16–17 and I wasn't much older at 24.

If you offer a friend a glass of your finest 25-year-old whiskey, and he puts coke in it, the next time around do you give him the same or the cheapest brand you have available? The guy who mixes your 25 year old whiskey with Coke isn’t supposed to be there in the first place. He’s your wife’s crazy younger brother who always needs money borrowed but always knows when you are having a party and invites himself over. He’s the in-law who doesn’t really know anybody in the room but wants to be the center of attention telling a bunch of ‘I-kid-you-not’ water cooler stories and never giving anyone else a chance to speak. Or he’s the eccentric neighbor who claims that they don’t drink alcohol but the minute they see the price tag of your 25 year old Glenfiddich, they want to try ‘just a little bit.’ When either of these characters come over my 25 year old bottle of whiskey is locked away securely in the liquor cabinet. When any of these guys show up to the party, Mr. Lawson becomes the drink of the evening.

What did someone do to their home that you just can't understand? My stepfather's parents owned a home that was a source of pride for the family. It was a rather large and stately hillside home that possessed several apartments on the bottom floor. The top floor was designed with several balconies that it could be used to host parties and events. The parents themselves had a good reputation with the neighborhood and kept the house in fine shape. They had three sons (one of which was my stepfather of course) all of whom couldn't be any more different than their parents in terms of reputation. When the parents died, they didn't make a will but rather implied to their sons that the oldest would be in charge while the younger ones would have living rights. At the times of their deaths the oldest was homeless and mentally unstable in Brooklyn after a long stint as a crack addict. The middle son (my stepfather), then used this opportunity to take reign, much to the displeasure of the youngest. He commanded the massive top floor to himself and rented the bottom floor apartments. At this time the area had become infused with drugs and crime and the house was starting to show signs of age. Deciding not to renovate it, (even though he's a skilled builder by trade) my stepfather decided to rent it to any old riffraff that comes by. In less than a year the house is infested with drug pushers, addicts, thugs and various people of ill repute whilst my stepfather sat like a Shantytown King overlooking everything from his balcony. The house started to become plagued with issues. Several of the toilets stopped working, many tenants had electrical issues, the front entrance was unusable as a a tree fell onto the front gate and destroyed it but was never removed, the cesspit was in dire need of flushing out so the entire house stank of this deep ghastly scent. The tenants decided to stop paying their rent. My stepfather, always a provocative individual, continuously hurled curses and threats towards his tenants for his rent money until one of them got fed up and assaulted him, threatening to kill him. My stepfather fled the house, never to return. The youngest son took this opportunity to have his daughter, a police woman, gather up her police friends and get rid of all the tenants. He took ownership of the house but by this time the house was so run down that he had no inspiration to do anything but reside on the top floor. He fell victim to lethargy and stopped paying bills and pretty soon the electricity was cut. He abandoned the house and lives with his daughter. The oldest son, deported and homeless, finally took residence in the dilapidated house. To answer the question as to what someone can do to their house that I just can't understand: I can't understand why parents would ever leave behind their house to be shared amongst the children.

What is the lamest “benefit” you’ve been offered by an employer? At Papa John’s Pizza (Trinidad) I was getting fed up that they weren't hiring the sufficient amount of staff to properly run the store. Along with doing bike deliveries I also cashed, took phone calls, entered orders, swept, mopped and emptied garbage. They kept a skeleton staff of 3 workers per shift and whenever they had to pay overtime they grumbled and wanted explanations as to why. Frustrated and fatigued I applied for Domino’s (Trinidad) Pizza delivery. This is how snippets of the conversation went during the interview. Interview Lady: We pay the highest hourly rate of all pizza restaurants. $21(TTD) per hour. Me: Papa John's paid $20 an hour. This is just a dollar more. Lady: Yes! The highest rate for delivery riders in the country! Lady: When you come to the restaurant you’ll be happy to see that you'll be getting so much deliveries. Endless deliveries! Me: How much do I get paid per delivery? Lady: $7 per delivery! Me: That's the lowest delivery payment of all the pizza restaurants. Lady: Yes but you'll be doing so many deliveries, getting so much tips that it wouldn't matter. (I later found out that Domino's charged customers $20 for delivery, the highest delivery charge of all fast food restaurants in the country. They paid the driver $7 out of the $20 charge and the restaurant pocketed the remaining $13 for themselves.) Me: What are the closing hours? Lady: 10:30pm. Me: You mean like only on Fridays and Saturdays? Lady: No every day. Me: Thats a bit late and taxis round here stop working around 8pm. Any transport provided for me to get home? Lady: No. Me: Will I be able to use the Domino's motorcycle to get home? (I was allowed this benefit in a previous restaurant I worked that had this same issue) Lady: No. Me: Can I leave earlier then? Lady: Of course. Due to your transport situation we’ll allow you to leave 10 minutes earlier! Lady: We are a very flexible organization. Me: How so? (inwardly groaning, expecting more bullshit) Lady: We give you the choice to work either as contracted or non-contracted. Me: What does that mean? Lady: Contracted means that you work somewhat as a permanent staff. You can work all the overtime hours you want. However overtime would be paid at the usual rate of $21 an hour. No time and a half. The same applies for public holidays. Non contracted is like temporary staff. We pay the usual time and a half for overtime but as you are non contracted you don't get overtime hours as we send you home after you've made your 40hrs a week. We don't allow you to work on holidays so you basically get your flat salary every week whereas with a contract you are allowed more hours. Me: More hours at the same rate? Lady: Yes. Me: Wouldn't that be a lose-lose situation? Lady: No. It's a win-win! Me: Am I entitled to a free meal? Lady: No. Me: And the uniform? Lady: We are the only pizza restaurant that provides free uniforms for staff? Me: How many uniforms? Lady: Two free Domino's shirts and a cap. We are having them laundered after being returned by a delivery driver who recently left. Me: You're giving me a guy's used clothes? No: No. She only used them for two days. They're practically new. Me: You're giving me used female clothing? Lady: It's a free uniform! Suffice to say I instantly and humbly returned to Papa John's and their skeleton staff. Edit: So as not to confuse anyone else, all rates here are in Trinidad dollars and not US. Approx 7TT = 1US. Edit: Not the first time a fast food restaurant tried to pull a fast one on its workers. Read here how one restaurant tried to borrow money from its workers in disguise.

What actor or actress got cast in a role that they normally wouldn't play and absolutely crushed it? Everyone I know who saw Along Came Polly (2004) agrees that the standout comedic performance was… not Ben Stiller (The Ben Stiller Show, There's Something About Mary, Meet The Parents etc) nor Jennifer Aniston (Friends, Office Space, Bruce Almighty) nor Hank Azaria (The Simpsons, Futurama, Mystery Men) nor Debra Messing (Will and Grace, Ned and Stacey) The person who outperformed these four seasoned and well known comedians with decades of experience in film and television (and they were all excellent) was this guy. Phillip Seymour Hoffman At that point in his career Hoffman did not have the level of acclaim as he does now. He was mostly known for his eccentric supporting roles in mostly dramatic films such as Boogie Nights, The Talented Mr. Ripley, Happiness and The Big Lebowski. Just a year after starring in this zany comedy he played the role of Truman Capote in the the film Capote (2005), won the Oscar for Best Actor and from then on his status soared with him being called the greatest actor of his generation. It helped that his role was that of washed up actor Sandy Lyle who believes himself to be of the highest pedigree (despite never having a single role since a hit comedy in the 80s). Hoffman nails it with his character’s sometimes pompous, sometimes laidback mannerisms. He makes it seem effortless in that unique, low-key Phillip Seymour Hoffman style of his It's a pity that he died in 2014, at the prime of his professional career. He was finally being truly recognized for his talent and given leading roles. In my honest opinion, his performance in Doubt (2008) is without a doubt his greatest performance. I'm of the view he even outstaged Meryl Streep in their scenes together. I would've loved to see him take on more comedic roles. I think that he put his heart and soul into his performances and added his own subtle nuances to his characters. Even if you are like critics and don't think much of Along Came Polly, it's hard to hate Hoffman's unforgettable performance as Sandy Lyle.

What Scorsese film would have been better if directed by Spielberg and vice versa? Interesting question. In regards to Spielberg doing a Scorsese film, I know I may be in a minority but I never had much love for Scorsese's Gangs of New York (2002). I've never been able to sit through the entire film. In my honest opinion, just because the epoch the film is based on is an ugly period in history, it doesn’t mean that the film has to be inherently ugly. In the comparable and far superior Once Upon A Time in America (1984), Sergio Leone captures the pockets of childhood innocence and warm camaraderie in a truly poetic manner despite the inherent ugliness of the period documented. In Gangs of New York everywhere looked like a filthy trash heap. All the main characters were assholes. Everyone was somehow dressed in the most rattiest rags they could find. I think Scorsese was a little heavy handed in demonstrating the chaotic grittiness of the period. With the exception of Daniel Day Lewis the entire cast gave mediocre performances. The colours and camera work of the cinematography was glaring and unsettling and the whole revenge arc story didnt seem to have much of a point in the context it was used. In a nutshell the film was just a pointless, ugly film that just happened to have a measure of historical accuracy. Spielberg is the King of demonstrating the humanity that can be found in the absolute darkest periods of history. He does this without undermining historical accuracy or succumbing to fluffy melodrama. Of course the chief examples being Schindler's List and Saving Private Ryan. I think if Spielberg was given the job to direct Gangs of New York, the final product would've been a superior film with fleshed out, relatable characters, a better plot and overall a much more engaging experience for the senses. In regards to Scorsese doing a Spielberg film, I think the there is one film that was right up Scorsese’s alley that I think Spielberg’s did a disservice. Scorsese's eye for realism and portraying characters in their raw, unlikable form would've created a better product. No. It's not Munich (2005) It's Catch Me if You Can. The film was a the feelgood blockbuster movie of 2002. Frank Abagnale Jr was the antihero everyone couldn’t help but love, especially when portrayed by hearthtrob Leonardo DiCaprio. I enjoyed the movie when it premiered but it has aged poorly as of recently. Abagnale Jr was not just a scammer, it has been revealed that he is also a pathological liar. Much of the events described in his book are either grossly exaggerated or completely untrue. When you watch the film now you are treated to a self-indulgent, ego-stroking feast of fakery. I think Scorsese would've been a bit more skeptical towards the author's story and do the proper research into Abagnale Jr's life. The story would've been less attractive and a lot more cynical with moments of downright nastiness (very much in the vein of Raging Bull and The Wolf of Wall Street) but it might have been a compelling portrait of a fractured individual who thought more of himself than he actually was. It definitely wouldn't have the embarrassment that Catch Me if You Can suffers from today. So in conclusion, Spielberg and Scorsese should’ve simply traded director seats in the year 2002.

Have you ever witnessed an office prank that cost someone their job? I may be cheating a bit but I can't help to answer such a burning question. I performed a prank that could've cost me my job. In my late teens I worked in a warehouse doing manual labor which mostly included picking up boxes of products, placing them on a trolley and bringing them to the front to be delivered. It could sometimes be rather monotonous especially when the huge orders came in and you spent all day rolling about the massive double warehouse in your creaky trolley that always had one bad wheel. Jason (or J as he preferred to be called) was our supervisor. He was a muscular guy with a deadpan face and shiny bald head. He was the butt of many of our jokes because he spoke in this forced, psudo-sexy whisper and constantly licked his lips while giving his daily inspirational morning speeches (we would call him LL Cool J in secret). He didn't have much of a sense of humour. He barely ever smiled and no one saw him laugh, although one of my friends claimed to have seen him laughing at an episode of Rugrats while behind his office computer. Anyways. As I mentioned the job could be monotonous. One evening I saw that one of the older female workers, Erica, had written on the bulletin board. 'I love my fellow workers.’ This irritated me because it was not a bulletin and it had an air of Soviet Communism about it. I wanted to change it to 'I love my fellow COMRADES' and draw a hammer and sickle but I knew that most of my coworkers wouldn't get the joke and it would be ignored. In the end I decided to change it to 'I love my fellow SLAVES.’ That would catch their attention and provide a good laugh and then it would be erased and teach Erica to stop using the bulletin board to write her insipid, brown-nosed statements. Unbeknownst to me J, who was of African descent, was in the process of watching all the episodes of Roots on DVD. He was emotionally charged about African history and slavery in particular. It didn't even occur to me that he was wearing a lot of African themed clothing also. The next morning I arrived just in time for the morning prayer and J's speech. The atmosphere was like a funeral as I entered the warehouse and saw everyone staring at me. J, in a low growl, asked me if I was the one who wrote the slave comment on the board. I replied yes. J licked his lips and made a long, impassioned plea about slavery and black pride. Every time I tried to explain to him that I didn't mean it in a context of race he would say, 'Shut up Jumbo (my nickname).’ He then ended by saying in his low psudo-sexy LL Cool J voice, 'Don't you ever………..ever, ever………let me see you write anything racist on this board again.’ Had I not been of African descent myself I'm certain I would've been put on extended probation, let go or at least spoken to by HR. My friends enjoyed the whole ordeal and it made good scuttlebutt for a few days. I never touched the bulletin board again but being the best impersonator of J, I was sought after by my friends and coworkers to re-enact J's racism speech. I would do a perfect impersonation with exaggerated licking lips and have them howling with laughter. Unfortunately I was called into Js office some time later. I was in trouble. Someone snitched to J that I was mocking how he spoke. I was certain now I would get the boot. Instead I saw J with a big smile on his face watching on his phone a video of me impersonating him. 'Jumbo,' he said and then licked his lips, 'Let me see you talk like me.’ I looked at him and repeated what he just said, licked lips and all. To my surprise he simply smiled and gave a soft 'he he he’ laugh and told me to go back to work and stop fooling around. He did have a sense of humour after all. Myself with some friends at the warehouse. J wasn't present unfortunately.
